about: sound CPU $4000-$7FFF and $C000-$FFFF: speech phrase table and TMS5220 data, tune table and tune data, speech command stubs and the speech driver, POKEY music player, envelopes, sound effect sequences and tables, effect stubs, mainline, IRQ, init, self test, the command table PBX and the vectors

S:FBAD.name: aud_tie_cannon
S:FBAD.desc: sound command $3D, Star Wars's AUDTC: starts the effect of table tab_xl (Atari's XL0, X-wing laser) with AUDNEW - chip 1 channel 2, chip 1 channel 3, about 3.3 s. Star Wars's AUDTC, the TIE fighter cannon, already used the X-wing laser data (switched for better effect, says Atari's comment)

S:FBB4.name: aud_tie_cannon_off

comments.S:C05E: tune data from here to $D936. a step is two bytes: a note number (0 = rest, else the index into NOTTAB once the key offset is added) and a duration ($40 a quarter note, $80 a half, $20 an eighth, $16 $16 $14 a triplet, bit 0 set = tied to the note before, 0 = end of the tune) - or a function $80-$91 and its value (table PKDT: $80 .NRATE, $81 .CRATE, $82 .NVOL, $83 .CVOL, $84 .NKEY, $85 .CKEY, $86 frequency envelope, $87 .AENV, $8A .VC, $8B POKEY control, $8C .SYN, $8D .CALL tune number, $8E .LOOP count, $8F .ENDL), $90 .GOSUB with a two byte address, $91 .RETURN alone
comments.S:C4F4: tune 15: the Imperial March, voice 1, the melody (.NVOL 9, .NRATE 60, .AENV 3), from .NRATE 120 on the march rhythm in triplets. tunes 15-18 are the four voices sound command $2B starts

comments.S:4000: checksum word of the first ROM, Star Wars's CKSUM0: with it TEST's sum of $4000-$5FFF and $C000-$DFFF comes out right
comments.S:E0A9: frequency envelope 2, which Star Wars does not have: the table of +1 steps after GLOCK
comments.S:E0AD: amplitude envelopes 1, 2 and 3: the table at $E1B3, EHARD and QKRIZE. Star Wars's fifth entry (TIES) is gone
comments.S:E0F3: not fill: frequency envelope 2, 64 steps of +1. a frequency envelope holds signed steps added to the note's divider (times 8 for the 16 bit music voices), indexed by half the voice's step count VSEQ, so POKSN can read 128 of them: envelope 1 (GLOCK, all -1) runs on into this table and this one into NULENV
comments.S:E1B3: amplitude envelope 1 (.AENV 1), where Star Wars has SDRUM: 32 signed bytes added to the voice's volume VVOL, one for each update of the voice (8 ms) from the start of an untied note, the last one held. this one starts at +10 and falls to -4
comments.S:E1D3: amplitude envelope 2 (.AENV 2), 32 bytes: +3, +7, then down to -1
comments.S:FA58: sound effect tables (Atari's OFFSET statements), read by AUDNEW: a mask byte, bit 7 = channel pair 0 down to bit 0 = pair 7 (pairs 0-3 are the four channels of POKEY chip 0, pairs 4-7 of chip 1), then for each set bit two addresses, the sequence for the frequency register and the sequence for the control register. questions: S:C639, S:C8AF, S:C92B: these three 'routines' are not code. the bytes are notes of tunes 15, 16 and 17 ($16 $39 $16 = two triplet notes, $20 $00 / $20 $80 = rests) that the orphan pass took for LBRA / BRA. the LBRA at $C639 'jumps' to $FF52, which is why the command table PBX from $FF52 to $FFD9 is listed as instructions. hints.py needs NOT_CODE for (S, $C639) and (S, $C92B) (and $C8AF, reached from $C92D), then PBX comes out as 82 words $FF4C-$FFEF. i gave no names to these three headers
S:FF52-S:FFD9 is data listed as code (see above). the regions and the per-entry comments i give for S:FF4C-S:FFEF apply once the false code is gone
S:FC6A (7 bytes shown as .byte) is code: LDY #$FB85 / JMP AUDNEW. nothing reaches it - PBX goes from $FC63 (command $50) to $FC71 (command $51). its table at $FB85 only silences chip 0 channel 1

S:FFF0: PBXS_EQ is $53 and both DOCMD (CMPB #$53 / BHI) and the self test sequence in MAIN (CMPB #$53 / BLO) accept command $52, but PBX has routines for $00-$51 only. the word used for $52 is $9CA7 at $FFF0, which by its place is the ROM's checksum word (TEST's two sums come out right with it) and points to no ROM. the main program does send $52 (its aud_cmd_52). what the sound CPU does at $9CA7 depends on what the board returns there and i could not settle it from the ROM - possibly the routine at $FC6A was meant, the one routine without a table entry. command $53 goes through the SWI3 vector to INIT

names carried from Star Wars that sit on the wrong routines (the matcher placed them by position - ESB dropped Star Wars's RY, RD, TL, RC, DR, RS and TH effects, which shifts the list). by the tables they load: S:FB8A AUDRY is Star Wars's AUDXL (loads BL0, command $3F), S:FB91 AUDRD is AUDPB (PB0, $35), S:FB98 AUDPH is AUDPBZ (PBZ0, $36), S:FB9F AUDRS is AUDSH (SH0, $3A), S:FBA6 AUDTH is AUDPF (PF0, $37), and S:FC55 AUDYEA, S:FC5C AUDNAY, S:FC63 AUDTST are new ESB effects (commands $4E, $4F, $50). i did not rename them, i put an esb_notes line on each and lower-case names on the true ones (aud_port_hole $FBDE, aud_yea $FBE5, aud_nay $FBEC, aud_test_tones $FBF3). these eight are candidates for sw_drop_names with the names AUDXL, AUDPB, AUDPBZ, AUDSH, AUDPF, aud_fx4e, aud_fx4f, aud_fx50. the carried symbols RY0 ($FAB2) and TST0 ($FB77) in sw_carry.json are wrong for the same reason

the PM routine names are right as code (same tune numbers as Star Wars) but ESB put other music behind most of them: PMEND plays the Imperial March, PMDAR the march's rhythm figure, PMTH5 still the main theme, PMREB is dead (empty tunes, no command). i left the names and added esb_notes

music i could not identify by ear from the data: command $29 (tunes 35-38), $2C (tunes 23-26) and $31 (tunes 31-34). command $30 (tunes 39-42) looks like Yoda's theme from its notes (C G C, A F#, G E C B, A in the written key) - not verified by listening. the uses i give for the tune commands come from the main program's calls of its stubs for $29-$31 (L711E, P1_95E5, L6E3A, L6FBD, L6BF0, L6991, L7494, L74B6)

speech: i can say which command says which phrase (comments on the rows at L4002) but not what the 41 phrases say - none of them has the same data as a Star Wars phrase. phrase 0 is never said (same data as phrase 1) and phrase 28 is a single byte no word list uses

carried Atari statement comments inside the tune data ($C098-$C74A, for example .NOTE lines in BENV1-BENV4 and in the first part of the Imperial March) were matched by byte runs, they describe the bytes correctly as statements but the surrounding .CALL / BENV5 comment lines are Star Wars's source and do not match ESB's longer tunes

the labels GLOCK, EHARD and QKRIZE carry Star Wars's statement comments (.BYTE lists) that already did not match the bytes in Star Wars. $E0F3 is listed as 'ROM fill, 64 bytes of $01' but is frequency envelope 2
effects of commands $41-$51: described by channels, control type and length only, the ROM does not say what they are for. S:F505-S:F5AD is a sequence pair no table uses

the per-table pointer regions ($FA59 up) start one byte after each table's mask byte, so each table becomes a .byte row for the mask and .word rows for the sequence addresses. labels and comments on tune starts that are now in the middle of a .byte row ($CB1C, $CB1E, $D092 and so on) rely on the row being split at the new TUNTAB pointer targets
